httpOnly.description:
Enables the [`HttpOnly` `Set-Cookie` attribute](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-5.2.6).
When enabled, clients will not allow client-side JavaScript to see the cookie in `document.cookie`.

maxAge.description: Get the max age in seconds, defaulting to 7 days

path.description:
Specifies the value for the [`Path` `Set-Cookie` attribute](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-5.2.4).
When no path is set, the path is considered the ["default path"](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-5.1.4).

sameSite.description:
Specifies the value for the [`SameSite` `Set-Cookie` attribute](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-09#section-5.4.7).

- `true` will set the `SameSite` attribute to `Strict` for strict same site enforcement.
- `'lax'` will set the `SameSite` attribute to `Lax` for lax same site enforcement.
- `'none'` will set the `SameSite` attribute to `None` for an explicit cross-site cookie.
- `'strict'` will set the `SameSite` attribute to `Strict` for strict same site enforcement.

More information about enforcement levels can be found in [the specification](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-09#section-5.4.7).

keysFile.description:
JSON file holding the keys, typically a mounted Kubernetes secret, instead of the registry

Same shape as the registry entry: `{ "current": "<id>", "key_<id>": { publicKey, privateKey, symetric } }`.
A relative path is resolved against the application path. Generate one with `webda crypto generate-keys`.

When set, the registry is never read nor written: `autoCreate` and `autoRotate` are ignored and
{@link CryptoService.rotate } fails. Rotate by adding a `key_<id>` to the file and switching `current`, keep
the previous keys as long as data encrypted with them must stay readable. The file is reloaded when it
changes, no restart needed.

autoTls.description:
Auto-generate a self-signed certificate on startup when `key`/`cert`
aren't configured. Dev convenience: gives the main port HTTP/2 via
ALPN (plus HTTP/1.1 fallback) with zero setup. Keys are written under
`.webda/dev-tls/`.

clientAuth.description:
Client certificate request on the TLS port: "none" does not ask for one, "optional" asks and accepts clients
without one or with an unverified one (see ClientCertificate.verified), "require" refuses the TLS handshake of
clients without a certificate signed by `clientCa`

Defaults to "optional" when clientCa is set, "none" otherwise

clientCa.description: CA file(s) used to verify client certificates — enables mTLS on the TLS port

clientCertHeader.description:
Header carrying the client certificate verified by a reverse proxy, disabled when undefined

Only accepted from `trustedProxies`: a request carrying it from another source is refused (400)

defaultHeaders.description:
Default headers to send to the client

Having a Cache-Control: private will prevent caching for API
If you overwrite this parameter, you will need to add it back

h2c.description:
Run this instance as an HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) server rather than
HTTP/1.1. The resulting port accepts only prior-knowledge HTTP/2
clients (e.g. `grpcurl -plaintext`). To serve both REST (HTTP/1.1)
and gRPC without TLS, configure a second HttpServer service with
`h2c: true` on a separate port.

healthPath.description:
Path of the readiness and liveness probe, disabled when unset

Answered before the routing, without a context: `200 {"status":"ok"}` once Core is ready, `503` while
it is starting (`{"status":"starting"}`) or the server is draining (`{"status":"stopping"}`).
The `WEBDA_HEALTH_PATH` environment variable enables it when not configured: the Knative deployer sets
it for the readiness probe of its revisions.

http2.description:
Enable HTTP/2 (default: true when key+cert provided)
Set to false for HTTPS without HTTP/2

key.description: TLS key file path — enables HTTPS or HTTP/2

port.description:
Port to listen on

When not set, the `PORT` environment variable is used (Knative, Cloud Run and most PaaS inject it),
then 18080. An explicit value always wins over the environment.

requestLimit.description:
Will not try to parse request bigger than this

This parameter can be overriden by a direct call to
getHttpContext().getRawBody(xxx)

requestTimeout.description:
Will not take more than this to read a request (unit: milliseconds)

This parameter can be overriden by a direct call to
getHttpContext().getRawBody(undefined, xxx)

shutdownGracePeriod.description:
Milliseconds the server waits for its in-flight requests when it stops, before closing their connections

Stopping first refuses new connections and answers `503` on `healthPath`, so a load balancer stops
routing to the instance. Keep it below the termination grace period of the pod (30s on Kubernetes).

Schema.description: Parameters for the in-memory FIFO queue, including message expiration and receive timeout

expire.description: Number of seconds before droping message

idleDelayer.description:
Delayer between two receives of the main consumer while the queue returns no message

Queues answering immediately when empty (PostgresQueue, AMQPQueue...) would otherwise be polled in a tight
loop. The delay grows with the consecutive empty receives, up to `maxIdleDelay`; the time spent in the receive
is deducted, so long-polling queues (SQSQueue, FileQueue, MemoryQueue with a timeout) are not slowed down.

maxConsumers.description:
Max number of queue consumers
Queue will auto increase to this max number if queue is loaded
and it will decrease to just one consumer if no messages are available

maxIdleDelay.description:
Maximum delay between two receives while the queue stays empty, in milliseconds

It bounds the extra latency of the first message after an idle period, and the polling rate of an idle
consumer (4 receives per second at 250ms).

timeout.description: Number of seconds to wait for receiving new message

workerDelayer.description: Delayer between two failed attempts to process messages

workerParallelism.description: Define if worker should process multi message received in //

Schema.description: TokenService parameters

refreshGrace.description:
Seconds during which a rotated refresh token presented again is rotated once more, as long as the token it was
exchanged for was never used: a client that lost the answer of its refresh (laptop asleep, network drop)
retries with the token it still holds instead of losing its session. The unused replacement is retired; if it
is presented later anyway (two holders), the family is revoked. 0 disables it: any replay revokes the family

revocationCacheTtl.description: Seconds a "not revoked" answer is cached: bounds how long a revocation done by another instance can be missed

revocationCheck.description: Reject access tokens whose family or user was revoked

MFA.description:
Multi-Factor Authentication behavior: second factors and recovery codes of the model holding it.

Actions are exposed as `<Model>.<Attribute>.<Action>`. The configured login attribute also completes
